test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && bash scripts/check-module-project-references.sh && python3 scripts/check-traceability.py --all && bash scripts/secret-scan.sh && (cd web && npx tsc --noEmit) && (cd tests/frontend && npx vitest run) && (cd tests/frontend && npx playwright test bio-int-004-webhooks)
notes:
Post-acceptance re-review remediation, not a fresh security round and not another acceptance cycle. Seyi re-reviewed the acceptance-rejection fix (commit 94c42be) and found its new Playwright suite's only 'failure' test proved a client-side guard (the create button disabling at zero event types), never a genuinely failed create/toggle API call with a visible error state - a silently swallowed error or an unhandled API 500 would have passed the suite unchanged. Fixed two ways. First, WebhookSubscriptionsPanel.tsx's own `notice` state now carries an explicit `isError` flag alongside its message, rendered with `role="alert"` only when it is one - mirroring the SAME role="alert" pattern this panel's own load-failure states (`error`/`offline`) already use, and the pattern every other panel in this codebase already establishes for a visible failure. Before this fix a failed create/toggle rendered through the identical plain

a successful one did - indistinguishable to an assistive-technology user, and nothing a test could tell apart from a silently swallowed error either. Second, a new Playwright test (`tests/frontend/playwright/bio-int-004-webhooks.spec.ts`) clears the URL input field while leaving an event type checked - bypassing the existing client-side zero-event-types guard entirely - so the create call genuinely reaches `createWebhookSubscriptionMockPort`'s own pre-existing 'A URL is required (SIMULATION)' validation failure (`web/features/bio-int-004/mock.ts`), a realistic domain-validation condition already present and reachable from the UI, not an invented magic-string trigger - the same convention `web/features/bio-crd-008/mock.ts` already established for this codebase. The test then asserts the notice carries `role="alert"`, contains the expected message, and that no new row or secret appeared - nothing silently succeeded. Also documented this round in docs/features/bio-int-004/README.md's own 'AC05 — web wiring' section and updated the story's top status line. No .NET source files were touched - this is a web-only change. Verified anyway for regression: dotnet build clean. 244/244 integration (one ObservabilityTests flake on the first run - the known pre-existing Console.Out-redirect race against concurrent WebApplicationFactory hosts, confirmed non-reproducing on immediate re-run, consistent with every prior occurrence this session). 210/210 unit, no regression. Module-reference/secret-scan/traceability all PASS. npx tsc --noEmit clean. npx vitest run 546/548 (the 2 failures are the pre-existing, already-tracked TD-BIO-UX-005-MODULE-REGISTRY-FIXTURE-GAP, unrelated). npx playwright test bio-int-004-webhooks: 6/6 passed (5 pre-existing plus the new failure-path test), re-run once more to confirm stability (both runs clean).
